mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or other government-issued identity document for each proposed director, officer and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague-convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the preceding 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague-convention states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening of all proposed directors, officers and UBOs against (i) the Canadian sanctions and listed persons administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act, (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and (iv) domestic Canadian law-enforcement watchlists. Foreign PEPs must be treated as higher-risk and trigger enhanced due diligence under FINTRAC guidelines; domestic/ provincial PEPs are assessed based on actual risk exposure. Adverse hits, sanctioned individual/prohibition findings, or unexplained source-of-wealth red flags requiring further enquiry shall result in refusal of the engagement and, where applicable, a Suspicious Transaction Report to FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire d'entreprise du Québec — Registraire des entreprises (online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); for federal CBCA incorporation, Corporations Canada online filing centre (https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate and firm names in Quebec must comply with the Charter of the French Language; the primary legal name must be legible and usable in French, and a non-French name is only permitted where it qualifies as a recognized mark or where the registrar accepts a distinct French version. All filings, name reservations and registry entries require Roman/Latin script; non-Roman script trade names must be transliterated into Roman characters and the transliteration must be supported by a certified sworn translation where relevant.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon official refusal, the applicant must first file a written administrative review request with the Registraire d'entreprise du Québec within 30 days of the refusal notice, attaching the official refusal certificate, the initial NUANS/name-search report, the proposed corrected name and a supporting legal memorandum explaining distinctiveness and non-confusion. If the administrative review is denied, judicial review may be sought before the Superior Court of Québec under the Code of Civil Procedure within the applicable limitation period; the registrar's name reservation is not renewable after its statutory validity window unless a new reservation application is filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a DTC e-commerce company only where the registered office is a physical commercial street address in Quebec at which process can be served physically during normal business hours; P.O. boxes and purely electronic addresses are prohibited. A serviced/virtual office arrangement with registered-agent reception and mail forwarding is acceptable for this business model; no physical retail or warehousing presence is required under ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% to 10% annualized likelihood for a standard low-risk internet-only retail corporation; unannounced on-site inspections are not routine but may occur following customer complaints, trademark/name disputes, tax verification, or targeted AML/CFT audits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c S-31.1, Sections 4 (incorporation), 10 (contents of articles), 16-17 (registration and certificate), 46-49 (registered office and records), 116-129 (directors and officers); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, Sections 21-28 (corporate names and public documents).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Direction de l'immatriculation des personnes morales
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) - REQ electronic filing form A-II
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; shares may be with or without par value and issued for any consideration fixed by the directors. No escrow or capital deposit account is required at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator's share subscription for the common shares set out in the Articles is adopted, and the Secretary shall issue the corresponding share certificates upon receipt of the agreed consideration. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is established at the address indicated in the Articles, and the Secretary shall file any changes with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed officers: President, Secretary and Treasurer, each to serve until replaced by the Board. RESOLVED, that the Corporation's by-laws are adopted and all lawful pre-incorporation acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation (Recherche et réservation de nom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the availability of the proposed corporate name against the central enterprise register; ensure the name complies with the French-language dominance rules under the Charter of the French Language; submit the name reservation request electronically and pay the CAD 42 reservation fee. The reservation is valid for 90 days and must be attached to the incorporation filing or replaced by a numeric designation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name components with legal designator (Inc., Corp. or French equivalents)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, file a new reservation with modified distinctive elements or request a written explanation from the REQ Director and seek judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec; alternatively adopt a numeric name (e.g. 1234-5678 Québec Inc.).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator, optionally assisted by a notary, for preparation prior to REQ filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation specifying the share structure (classes, rights, options, par or no-par value), the number of directors, any restrictions on share transfers, and the initial registered office address in Quebec. The incorporator must sign the articles; if the filing is made electronically, the REQ's accepted electronic signature method may be used.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate or numeric name election
Consent of each founding director to act as director (form or declaration included in the articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the identified inconsistencies and resubmit; if a notarial deed is required due to special conditions or restrictions, re-execute the articles before a Quebec notary and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with REQ and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed Articles of Incorporation through the REQ online portal, pay the CAD 322 statutory incorporation fee, and obtain the certificate of incorporation (attestation de constitution) together with the nine-digit Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). The corporation legally comes into existence on the date of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of the statutory incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: REQ issues a notice of deficiency; correct and resubmit the filing within the stated period. Any refusal to issue the certificate may be contested before the Superior Court of Quebec under the QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organization Meeting and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt a written resolution signed by all directors covering: adoption of by-laws (règlements administratifs), appointment of officers, issuance of subscriber shares, opening of corporate bank accounts, selection of the fiscal year-end, and ratification of pre-incorporation acts. Maintain the corporate minute book and securities register at the Quebec registered office.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes or written resolutions
Bank account opening resolution and KYC documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If organization is not completed, any director may convene a remedial meeting; missing corporate records must be reconstructed and signed retroactively by all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Quebec Establishment Filing (Revenu Québec, CRA and REQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec; Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); REQ for the establishment declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the Canada Revenue Agency for GST/HST (mandatory when the CAD 30,000 taxable-supply threshold is exceeded, or voluntarily earlier); register with Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (T.V.Q.) and, if employees exist, for payroll deductions and the CNESST workplace injury insurance account; file the Quebec establishment (établissement) declaration with REQ within 30 days of commencing commercial activity in the province.
required_dossiers: Estimated annual sales and payroll data
Platform sales statement from Shopify, PayPal and Stripe for threshold assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations may be backdated; where a reporting obligation was missed before any enforcement notice, submit voluntary disclosure to Revenu Québec and the CRA to request penalty relief.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the DTC webstore (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110) is a non-industrial digital retail activity and requires no manufacturing license. If the company later adds warehousing or light assembly operations, the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) and municipal industrial zoning authorities would govern those activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for a pure retail webstore; the only mandatory operational registrations are the REQ enterprise file and the Quebec establishment declaration. A municipal business permit (permis d'affaires) may be required by the local municipality depending on the registered office address.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - non-industrial category; e-commerce-only operations fall below the mandatory registration threshold of the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review, and no certificate of authorization is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no regulated wastewater, VOC or atmospheric discharge points exist at a digital storefront. Packaging and electronic waste obligations are governed by extended producer responsibility (EPR) regimes administered by Éco Entreprises Québec; if a fulfillment facility is later opened, municipal wastewater by-laws and CNESST occupational standards apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a digital storefront with no public access or industrial equipment. Office lease premises must comply with the Quebec Construction Code and fire safety provisions enforced by the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ). Upon hiring the first employee, the corporation must register with the CNESST for occupational health and safety and adopt a workplace prevention program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) is the federal tax authority; Revenu Quebec is the provincial tax authority for Quebec (QST, provincial corporate income tax). Primary portals are CRA My Business Account (canada.ca) and Revenu Quebec Business Online Services (CleNumerique).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity must first obtain a Business Number (BN) by registering with the CRA using Form RC1 or through the Business Registration Online service, identifying the entity type and income tax account. If the entity will make taxable supplies in Canada, it must also open a GST/HST program account (RT). For provincial nexus with Quebec, registration with Revenu Quebec is required for QST via Form LM-101-V, and the Quebec Registraire d'entreprises will issue an enterprise number (NEQ) which integrates with the provincial TIN system. The BN serves as the federal TIN; the QST account number (TD-QST) serves as the provincial indirect tax identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not use check-the-box elections. Canadian corporations are automatically treated as separate taxable entities. Statutory elections relevant to hybrid arrangements include the section 216 election (non-resident net-income election for rental and royalty income) and the section 142.4 mark-to-market election. For GST/HST, a joint election under section 150 may be used for certain financial services supplies. Hybrid mismatch rules under BEPS Action 2 apply by operation of law and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annual worldwide taxable supplies for GST/HST; the Quebec QST small-supplier threshold is likewise CAD 30,000. A non-resident DTC seller must register once total gross revenue from taxable supplies exceeds this threshold, subject to the simplified e-commerce rules for non-resident suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping of invoices. Electronically issued invoices are valid if they meet statutory content requirements under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec QST Act. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing framework exists to facilitate interoperable B2B exchange, but adoption is voluntary and no prior tax authority authorization or transaction-level clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under GST/HST applies to supplies of goods that are exported by the supplier, supplies of services performed wholly outside Canada for non-residents, and certain intellectual property transactions. For Quebec QST, similar zero-rating rules apply. A DTC webstore selling physical goods to foreign consumers qualifies when the goods are delivered to a destination outside Canada and proof of export is retained. Digital services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated where the recipient is outside Canada and the service is not performed for use primarily in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A or electronic CARM declaration)
Bill of Lading and/or Air Waybill evidencing international carriage
Proof of foreign currency receipt and inward remittance documentation
Carrier or freight forwarder certificates of export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where export documentation is incomplete or non-compliant, CRA and Revenu Quebec may claw back zero-rated treatment, reassess GST/HST and QST at the full import-tax equivalent (through reverse charge in Quebec), and charge interest and penalties. False statement penalties of the greater of CAD 100 and 5% of the tax, and gross negligence penalties of 50% of the tax evaded, apply. Criminal tax evasion can result in fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years. Revenu Quebec may impose parallel administrative penalties and pursue separate recovery.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential banking regulator; FINTRAC as financial intelligence and AML/ATF supervisor; the Department of Finance as lead on monetary and exchange-rate policy. Canada has no standalone foreign-exchange administration body; Banking Act and Currency Act govern monetary settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations: both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully and freely convertible. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a free-floating currency with no exchange-control approval, quotas, or surrender requirements. Profit-remittance hurdles are tax-driven, not FX-driven: dividends, interest, royalties, and management fees paid to non-residents are subject to Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) withholding (statutory 25%; treaty-reduced to 5–15% under most DTAAs, including the Canada–US treaty for direct dividends and arm's-length interest), with Quebec's supplementary provincial withholding coordinated through the Canada–Quebec tax collection agreement. No prior regulatory clearance, balance-of-payments approval, or documentary endorsement is required before wiring out dividends, repaying shareholder loans, or remitting royalties. Operationally, all wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more routed through Canadian banks are reported to FINTRAC as electronic funds-transfer reports (EFTRs); this is a supervisory reporting obligation, not a convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose any statutory timeline for export-proceeds repatriation nor any mandatory conversion ratio for export or retail DTC receipts. Proceeds may be held in CAD or foreign-currency treasury accounts without penalty. Tax compliance, however, requires: (i) realized and unrealized FX gains on business receivables/payables are recognized as ordinary income under general business principles (ITA s. 9), while foreign currency held as capital property is governed by ITA s. 39; (ii) a corporation may elect a functional currency under ITA s. 261 to defer conversion noise, but must file consistently for Canadian tax purposes; (iii) inward EFTs over CAD 10,000 trigger the bank's FINTRAC EFTR filing; (iv) specified foreign property exceeding CAD 100,000 must be reported on Form T1135; and (v) if the Canadian entity holds 10% or more of a foreign affiliate, Form T1134 must be filed annually.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: RBC Royal Bank (Royal Bank of Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — CAD/USD dual-currency treasury package with global wire desk
Operational Account — international trade desk, USD clearing, and e-commerce payment receivables

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account — Quebec-chartered presence, strong francophone corporate desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium as a supplementary collection/disbursement rail; Low as the sole treasury cash-management solution. Canada does not recognize the European 'Electronic Money Institution' (EMI) licence as a banking-equivalent class. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex may operate in Canada only by registering as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) under the PCMLTFA and by complying with the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), which entered into force in phases in 2024 and requires payment-service providers to register with the Bank of Canada by September 2025. Legal constraints: (i) an offshore EMI cannot open a Canadian settlement account in the EMI's own name for card-network clearing; (ii) Shopify Payments, Stripe, and PayPal Business each require settlement into a Canadian-chartered bank account or their own branded balance; (iii) incoming CAD settlement from an EMI may be treated as a third-party transfer by the Canadian bank, triggering additional source-of-funds review; (iv) USD clearing is typically executed through Canadian correspondent banks, adding 1–2 business days' settlement lag. Recommended architecture: hold the primary operational and capital accounts at a Schedule I bank and use one registered EMI solely for marketplace receivables collection and high-frequency cross-border vendor payments under separate client money segregation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for Canadian-incorporated corporations without mandatory physical attendance of directors, provided the 25%-or-greater beneficial owners and authorized signatories complete a live video-identification interview with a bank compliance officer. All major Canadian banks accept electronic submission of the certificate of incorporation (federal or Quebec), articles, registered-office notice, initial shareholder register, and corporate resolution, followed by a simultaneous video call. Non-resident directors are subject to enhanced due diligence: banks will request a valid passport, proof of residential address, a banking reference (where a local banking relationship exists), and confirmation of the Canadian registered office. In Quebec specifically, banks may request the French-language corporate name declaration or a translation of the resolution where the operating documents are in English. In practice, no director or shareholder needs to appear physically in Canada; a notarized authorization executed abroad, a Canadian-resident authorized signatory, and a video KYC interview will satisfy onboarding for a low-risk DTC e-commerce entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner(s) residing in a non-FATF or FATF grey-list jurisdiction combined with concentrated 100% shareholding in a single individual.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles of incorporation, initial share register, register of directors, registered-office certificate, government-issued photo ID and proof of residential address for the BO, bank reference from the shareholder's domestic financial institution, notarized source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement (executed in the home jurisdiction), a capital-subscription share purchase agreement, and current Shopify storefront URL plus inventory/supplier contracts demonstrating a live operating business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material mismatch between declared projected transaction volume and initial capital base (e.g., first-year revenue forecast above CAD 5 million without commensurate inventory purchase orders or marketing spend).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month cash-flow forecast; Shopify Payments and Stripe merchant statements covering the prior 6–12 months; supplier proforma invoices and purchase orders; bill of lading or customs-entry documentation; 3PL warehouse agreement or Québec business-lease; digital-advertising contracts (Meta Ads, Google Ads); domain ownership certificate; executed refund/chargeback policy; and corporate tax roll-forward (where prior-year T2 filed).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection originating from a jurisdiction with strict capital controls or from crypto-currency conversions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully documented share-subscription agreement; bank SWIFT MT103 evidencing fiat conversion through a licensed MSB; home-country central-bank or SAFE capital-control clearance; an AML-compliant source-of-funds report with a blockchain forensics certificate (e.g., Chainalysis) if any crypto intermediary was used; a Canadian legal opinion confirming the funds are not derived from sanctions-listed persons or mixers; and a signed indemnity/director's certificate flowing into the corporate minute book. Most Schedule I banks will reject crypto-derived capital unless the fiat conversion occurred via a registered Canadian crypto-to-fiat dealer and complete traceability is provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supplier base concentrated in sanctioned or high-risk trade corridors (e.g., payments to Chinese contract manufacturers, Hong Kong agents, or South American fulfilment partners) triggering false-positive sanctions screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete supplier register with legal-entity name, country of incorporation, SWIFT BIC, bank account jurisdiction, and sanctions-status confirmation; OSFI consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN, and UN-screening results; product HS/COO commodity codes; purchase orders and vendor attestations confirming goods are not dual-use or embargoed; escalation path for acceptable false-positive resolution; and a signed beneficiary declaration permitting the Canadian bank to share the supplier KYC package with the correspondent bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital is wired via SWIFT MT103 directly from the non-resident shareholder's account to the Canadian entity's CAD operational account, referencing the share-subscription agreement and using the Canadian transit/account number plus the bank's SWIFT BIC. Use the IMF Balance of Payments purpose code for direct-investment equity ('Equity – direct investment') for share capital, and code 'Other investment – loans' for shareholder advances. The Canadian bank files an FINTRAC EFTR for any credit of CAD 10,000 or more; no prior Bank of Canada or FINTRAC approval is required. For equity injections, the issuer must contemporaneously issue shares and record paid-up capital; for shareholder loans, a written demand or term loan agreement with a market-rate interest coupon (substantiated under ITA ss. 15, 80.4, and 247) must be executed and retained. For transfers above CAD 100,000, banks typically require an accountant's or lawyer's closing confirmation letter identifying the purpose, journal entry, and source of funds before same-day release to operating liquidity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails are layered for a Shopify DTC brand: (i) card-network settlements (Visa/Mastercard/Amex) are collected through Shopify Payments, Stripe, or PayPal and deposited into the Canadian corporate account in CAD by default; USD-denominated settlement can be directed to a CAD/USD multi-currency account where the platform supports split payout; (ii) supplier payments in foreign currency are executed via SWIFT MT103 with corresponding trade purpose codes (e.g., 'imports of goods' with commercial invoice reference); (iii) Payroll, dividend, and recurring vendor payments in CAD are cleared through Payments Canada's Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) and Lynx (large-value transfer system) for amounts above the high-value threshold; (iv) a Commercial Letter of Credit is permissible but unnecessary for typical DTC inventory purchases; telegraphic transfer (T/T) with sight payment is the prevailing rail; (v) each outbound wire over CAD 10,000 is reported to FINTRAC as an EFTR by the bank, and underlying commercial invoices must be retained in the transfer-pricing file to support ITA s. 247 arm's-length compliance and any cross-border excise/GST/HST alignment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward (plain vanilla) in CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/CNH with a Schedule I bank or designated FX dealer; tenors up to 24 months without Bank of Canada approval.
Rolling/extendable forward (flexible forward) to hedge uncertain e-commerce payout volumes from Shopify Payments and PayPal; executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or bank FX master agreement.
FX swap (swap-points transaction) between CAD and USD, or CAD and other G10 currencies, with T+2 spot start or same-day value where counterparty credit lines permit.

Cross-currency interest-rate swap (CCS/CIRS) to hedge long-term intercompany loans between the Canadian operating company and a foreign parent or subsidiary, subject to IFRS 9 hedge accounting designation.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for emerging-market currency exposures (e.g., offshore CNY, INR, BRL) with international counterparties; permissible for corporate hedging where an onshore deliverable market is unavailable.

OTC vanilla currency options (calls/puts) for asymmetric hedging of marketing-spend and supplier-payment contingencies; premium and collateral arrangements acceptable under Canadian securities law for commercial hedgers.
Spot FX contracts (T+2 value) for immediate supplier settlement; unrestricted execution through any OSFI-regulated bank or registered Canadian MSB/dealer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the corporation's incorporation or continuation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No immediate daily penalty, but failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Director to initiate administrative dissolution; struck-off corporations must apply for revival and pay arrears and reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the anniversary date of the enterprise's registration in Quebec; must be filed annually for as long as the enterprise is registered.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers tariffed late fees; failure to file for two consecutive registration years may lead to notice of strike-off, cancellation of the enterprise registration and, for a legal person, administrative dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a non-distributing CBCA or Quebec corporation, an independent audit is mandatory only for reporting/distributing corporations. A private corporation with fewer than 15 shareholders may waive the auditor appointment by unanimous shareholder consent for the year; otherwise an auditor must be appointed at the annual meeting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public/reporting issuers; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for the typical private DTC webstore corporation. Financial statements are reconciled to tax accounting in the T2 corporate income tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the CBCA, the corporation must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control and update it within 15 days of becoming aware of a change; the annual shareholder resolution or minutes should confirm the register is current. In Quebec, the annual declaration requires the enterprise to confirm and update information on directors, shareholders and, where applicable, individuals with significant control; all share transfers must be recorded in the transfer ledger and any resulting beneficial-ownership change reflected in the declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$200–US$700 per annum for a Quebec registered office and corporate agent arrangement.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000–US$15,000 per annum for a full statutory audit by a Quebec CPA firm; lower for a review engagement.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (federal Part I general rate 15% plus Quebec general corporate rate 11.5%), imposed at the entity level on a Business Corporation. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) benefits from a combined small business rate of 12.2% (federal 9% plus Quebec 3.2%) on the first C$500,000 of qualifying active business income derived from the Shopify DTC store.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for e-commerce. Preferential mechanisms: (1) federal Small Business Deduction and Quebec deduction pour PME reduce the effective rate to 12.2% on active business income up to C$500,000 (federal business limit is reduced when combined taxable capital of associated corporations exceeds C$10 million); (2) refundable SR&ED investment tax credits (federal 35% for CCPCs and Quebec parallel credit on eligible R&D salaries); (3) intercorporate dividend deduction under s.112; (4) availability of loss carryback (3 years) and carryforward (20 years). A corporation controlled by non-resident shareholders cannot qualify as a CCPC and loses the small business deduction.
